name: Aval Nanachathu
steps: Rinse the flattened rice very briefly and drain thoroughly. Leave it 5 minutes so the flakes soften without disintegrating; use a medium thickness rather than the very thin uncooked-poha type.
Dissolve grated jaggery in the measured warm water, strain if gritty, and stir in cardamom and a tiny pinch of salt. This should be a light coating, not a pool of syrup.
Toss the softened aval with fresh grated coconut and the jaggery liquid. Fold gently until every flake is lightly coated.
Cover for 10 minutes so the coconut and jaggery moisture penetrates the aval. Slice bananas just before serving to avoid browning.
Divide into four bowls and top with banana slices. Serve at room temperature; this is a moist, sweet breakfast, not a cooked porridge.
tips: Adjust softness with a tablespoon of water only if the flakes remain hard after resting.
passiveTime: Rest the dressed flattened rice for 10 minutes.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
